diagnostics.message: module.emr_on_eks:resource.null_resource.update_trust_policy: explicit depends_on of module.emr_on_eks:resource.aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution is redundant — already implied by attribute references
module.emr_on_eks:resource.null_resource.update_trust_policy: explicit depends_on of module.emr_on_eks:resource.kubernetes_namespace.spark is redundant — already implied by attribute references

module.aws_eks_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng: explicit depends_on of module.aws_eks_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_iam_role.managed_ng is redundant — already implied by attribute references

module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng: explicit depends_on of module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_iam_instance_profile.self_managed_ng is redundant — already implied by attribute references

module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng: explicit depends_on of module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_iam_role.self_managed_ng is redundant — already implied by attribute references

The aws-eks-teams module creates Kubernetes resources (kubernetes_namespace.team, kubernetes_cluster_role/team, kubernetes_role/team, kubernetes_service_account/team, kubectl_manifest.team) that can only be applied once the EKS cluster API endpoint is reachable. Every other module in this root that touches the Kubernetes API (module.aws_eks_managed_node_groups, module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups, module.aws_eks_fargate_profiles, module.emr_on_eks) declares `depends_on = [kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth]` — which is itself gated on the `data.http.eks_cluster_readiness` health check — but module.aws_eks_teams has no such dependency. Inside the module, resources like kubernetes_namespace.team reference only var.application_teams, so nothing orders them after cluster creation; a apply could try to create namespaces/roles before the cluster exists (or before the API server is healthy) and fail.

The explicit `depends_on = [module.aws_eks.cluster_id, ...]` entry on kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth is already implied transitively: aws_auth depends on data.http.eks_cluster_readiness, which depends on data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster, which depends on module.aws_eks. The module.aws_eks depends_on entry adds no ordering beyond what the readiness check already establishes.

The explicit `depends_on = [module.aws_eks.cluster_id, ...]` entry on kubernetes_config_map.amazon_vpc_cni is already implied transitively via data.http.eks_cluster_readiness -> data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster -> module.aws_eks. The module.aws_eks depends_on entry adds no ordering beyond the readiness-gated dependency.

The explicit `depends_on` entry for aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution on null_resource.update_trust_policy duplicates a dependency already established by the attribute reference to aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution.id in the local-exec command.

The explicit `depends_on` entry for kubernetes_namespace.spark on null_resource.update_trust_policy duplicates a dependency already established by the attribute reference to kubernetes_namespace.spark.id in the local-exec command.

The explicit `depends_on` entry for aws_iam_role.managed_ng on aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng duplicates the implicit dependency already created by `node_role_arn = ... aws_iam_role.managed_ng[0].arn`. (The depends_on entry for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.managed_ng is NOT redundant and should be kept, since policy attachment is not otherwise ordered before node-group creation.)
